note: ep08 vertical (2026-10-31): the whole episode as a standalone 9:16 Short, under 3 minutes, built because a small channel's reach comes from Shorts (decisions/0005). It must make sense to someone who has never seen the channel, so it names the loan, explains every chart out loud, and carries its own assumption panel. Replay lines carry `year` (years since signing) and scene r93 or r72. Speakers: N narrator, M Minh, L Lan, T Uncle Tu. Every spoken number is checked by tools/validate-ep08-story.mjs. `*word*` = emphasis. The family are illustrations.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: A *four hundred thousand dollar* mortgage at seven percent, and an extra *eight hundred dollars* a month. Pay off the house early, or invest it?

lines.speaker: L
lines.text: Send it to the bank. The house is ours in about sixteen years, not thirty.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Or put it in stocks. They should beat seven percent.

lines.speaker: T
lines.text: No debt, ever.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So let's replay it on real history. Same loan, same eight hundred, same rate, about *seven point four percent*. Two real start dates. On top, Lan pays down. On the bottom, Minh invests.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: June nineteen ninety-three.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Two thousand. Stocks are flying. *A hundred twenty-six thousand* invested!

lines.speaker: L
lines.text: Two thousand nine. My house is paid off.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Two crashes later, I've got the same *hundred twenty-six thousand*. And I still owe a hundred ninety-four.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Twenty twenty-three. Both houses are paid off. Lan has seven hundred forty-six thousand, Minh seven hundred ten. Paying down wins, by *thirty-six thousand*.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Now the same rate, twenty-one years earlier. September nineteen seventy-two.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Nineteen seventy-four. The market crashed. I've got *eleven thousand*.

lines.speaker: L
lines.text: Nineteen eighty-eight. My house is paid off!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I still owe a hundred two thousand. But I've got a hundred seventy-nine thousand invested.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Two thousand two. Minh has five hundred eighty-seven thousand, Lan two hundred sixty-five. Investing wins, by about *three hundred twenty thousand*.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Same rate. Opposite winners. So we ran every month since eighteen seventy-one: *fifteen hundred and six* thirty-year loans, all at seven percent. That's a what-if, but the stock history is real. Blue means investing ended up ahead. Red means paying down did.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Investing ended up ahead about *seven times in ten*. When it won, it usually won by about a hundred twenty thousand dollars. When it lost, it usually lost by about sixty thousand.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Now change only the rate. Each bar is one mortgage rate. The longer the bar, the more often investing came out ahead. At five percent or lower: every single time. At six: more than nine in ten. At seven: about seven in ten. At eight: *less than half*. The higher the rate, the more paying it off saves you.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: And their son Bin holds up a napkin.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Half and half? About two times in three, it ended between the other two. But about one time in four, it ended with *less money than both*.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So your rate decides. Around seven percent, investing usually won, but only if you invest every month, through every crash. Paying down is the smaller, surer win.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: What we assumed: stocks are the S and P with dividends, no fees. No taxes, no refinancing. The family are illustrations. The history is real. This is history, not advice.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: What's your rate? Lan's bank, or Minh's stocks? Tell me in the comments.
